content.thinking:
I'm planning the monster truck's proportions carefully in pixel art scale—roughly 3.5m tall tires, 5m length, 3.6m width—and setting up the chassis joint structure to build from.

Now I'm working out the hinge joints for the four wheels and front steering, plus hinged doors, and figuring out tire geometry: cylinders oriented along the X-axis with tread blocks built as merged box geometries around the circumference for a chunky pixel look.

For placement, I'm setting hub height around 0.84-0.85 for the 0.85-radius tires, axle positions at roughly ±1.45 in x and ±1.6 in z for the wheelbase, giving a monster-truck-style stance about 3.85 m wide. I'm also sketching the raised pickup body sitting above the axles -- chassis rails around y 1.1-1.3, body bottom near 1.35-1.5, cab top near 2.7 -- while checking that the body width doesn't awkwardly overlap the inner tire faces.

Resolving that overlap by narrowing tire width and nudging axle x outward so the inner tire faces clear the body sides, landing on a stance around 4 m wide. For the body panels I'm planning to use tileBox with a 5cm texel pixel texture for painted metal panels, then favoring cellPaint-based gradient shading on box geometries (snapping colors by height/normal for lighting) over complex tile art, plus decals for flames, numbers, and stripes.

Designing the flame decal as a procedural shape based on z-distance from the front, using a sine/triangle wave to vary flame height along the body, with orange outer and yellow inner color ramps, applied only to the side and front-facing panels of the body boxes.

Now I'm laying out the chassis structure: dark side rails running the length of the frame, crossmembers, front and rear axle rods with radius, and coil-over shock/spring assemblies angled between the axles and chassis mounts on each side.

Writing spring coil geometry...

I'll skip the tilt and use vertical shocks for the spiral sweep, attaching it to the root bone. For the body, I'm laying out the underbody pan as a dark box and starting on the cab's main box dimensions.

Still defining truck body geometry...

Simplifying to a four-point convex profile for the cab with a slanted back, then placing the windshield as a sloped plane on the angled front face.

Setting the plane's up vector and sizing it to 1.7 by 0.894, then working out the window frame proportions so the glass area leaves a margin within the texture.

Now I'm positioning the side windows on the cab's trapezoid profile, calculating where the slanted windshield and rear window lines intersect at different heights to get proper z-ranges, then placing the rear window plane facing backward and a side window plane facing outward.

For the pickup bed, I'm planning the floor as the top of the lower body box, adding side and back walls at a set height above it, plus a roll bar with glowing light squares and a roll cage made of rods over the bed. I'm also considering how the fenders/arches need to let the tires poke through the body sides.

I'm checking the tire and body proportions so wheels sit beside the chassis without overlapping, giving it a monster-truck stance since the body floor sits well above the axle line. Now I'm adding the front bumper, grille texture, and headlight glow squares onto the front face of the lower body.

I'm also figuring out exhaust stacks placed near the hood as angled chrome rods with a small glow flame at the tip, plus planning side mirrors, door handles, and seam lines for the doors.

For the doors, I'm setting up hinge joints at the front edge of each door (vertical axis), with thin door panel boxes attached to those hinge bones, sized to fit the cab's side height and positioned slightly outside the cab surface.

Refining the door dimensions to span z -0.85 to 0.28 and extending full height to match the cab front, then placing a window on the upper portion centered around y 2.5 with the lower door section below it.

The flame paint should continue consistently across both the lower body panels and the doors since they're painted as one unit. Now I'm thinking about adding a pixel-art decal to the door, like a roundel with a number, and sketching out 3x5 glyph rows for the digits.

Still writing digit pixel data...

I'm also planning a racing stripe decal on the hood, applying white/black paint based on the surface axis and position so it reads as a centered stripe.

For body coloring, I'm setting up a red color ramp with snapped hex shades, computing brightness from height and surface normal so the hood top reads brighter than the sides, with some dithering noise mixed in for texture.

Now I'm working out the flame decals on the side panels using a sawtooth-based tongue function so the flame tips taper backward from the front, with height decreasing and jaggedness increasing with distance, clamping to a base cutoff so only the upper region shows flame, then shading by depth within the flame shape.

Also defining a dark rocker skirt below the flame band, verifying the cell-paint approach works on the extruded cab geometry, and sketching out the wheel geometry—cylindrical tires with speckled rubber shading and tread blocks along the axis.

Now working out the lug geometry: staggered rows of small boxes around the tire radius for chunky tread detail, merged per wheel to keep triangle counts reasonable, and adjusting the tire core/lug radii so the overall wheel outer radius and hub height line up correctly with the ground.

Next I need to add rim and sidewall detail, maybe using a lathe-style cylinder for the rim with painted sidewall texture for extra realism.

Skipping full lettering, I'll simplify to a dashed white ring pattern on the sidewall, computed by radial distance from the hub and modulated by angle to create the dash effect.

Still writing wheel geometry...

So the wheel joint aims forward with dir [0,0,1] at the hub, and the steering joint sits at the same hub position aimed up [0,1,0] for Y-axis steering rotation. I'm laying out the joint hierarchy now: chassis as root, then steerFL/FR as children, wheelFL/FR/RL/RR, and doorL/doorR, with rear wheels parented directly to root.

I'm adding a tailgate hinge at the back of the bed, positioned at the top rear with a thin box piece for the actual tailgate panel, plus the bed's side walls. I'll skip suspension joints since they're not essential, and I'm planning a small lightbar box on the cab roof.

Still adding roof details and roll cage structure...

For headlights I'm using glow boxes with warm yellow-white tones layered under a chrome bezel, positioned at the front plane. I'm working out the front bumper and grille placement, stacking the hood lip, grille block, and bumper box at slightly different heights and depths to get the proportions right.

Now I'm adding push bar rods running vertically from the bumper to the hood, a small winch cylinder, and red tow hooks for detail. For the cab interior, since the body is solid, I'll fake depth by drawing darker silhouette shapes into the window texture itself, like a seat headrest outline, combined with a dark gradient and diagonal highlight stripes to suggest glass reflection.

I'll also stamp a small helmet silhouette into the windshield texture for the driver, using a red and black palette for the helmet and visor, placing it on the correct side depending on which way the model's left/right axis corresponds to the viewer's perspective.

Checking texel density across the shared paint sheet, roughly 70 m² of painted surface at 1024 resolution gives about 1cm per texel, so bumping paintSize to 2048 keeps the 3-5cm cells crisp. I'm also verifying tire hub heights keep the bottom resting right at y=0, and confirming the 14-sided cylinder tires have enough triangles to look round.

Now I'm planning the extra details: spring shocks, axles, differential, driveshaft, chassis rails, and a supercharger poking through a hood scoop with chrome intake pipes. I'm also adding rivet rows along the fender lines using merged boxes, a running board along the belly, and chrome side exhaust pipes positioned between the front and rear wheel wells so they don't clip the tires.

I'm now thinking about amber side marker lights, a thin antenna rod with a small flag pennant, and whether to add a decal like flames or a pixel skull emblem on the hood. For the skull decal I'm working out the plane orientation so it reads correctly from the front camera's viewpoint, deciding which way "up" should face so the image isn't upside down.

Designing pixel skull pattern...

Verifying row widths...

Now I'm moving to writing the actual code, being careful about which imports are actually used to avoid unused import errors.

Setting up the builder and helper functions for box geometry placement...

Defining color palettes for the paint job...

Still refining the flame geometry formula...

Finishing the color gradient logic...tongue base yellow fading to red tips, checking whether flames reach the door panels and hood faces given each part's z-position and amplitude. Flames mostly stay on belly and fender since door amplitude is low, but hood amplitude is high enough to show flames, so I'm bumping the base amplitude up to 1.05 for better visibility.

Now I'm defining the rubber color palette and tire paint function, setting up sidewall rings with red bands and white lettering based on radius ranges from the rim outward.

Adding more tire geometry...

Still building wheel geometry...

I'm working out the axle rod dimensions, keeping it hidden inside the tire core so only the exposed portion near the hub is visible, plus adding steering knuckle boxes at the hub and a flattened differential sphere for the axle housing.

Now I'm placing the suspension linkages — panhard rods and four-link bars connecting the axle to the chassis — then setting up vertical shocks and springs at each wheel position with appropriate steel rod radii.

Writing spring geometry...

Working out the door seam by layering a slightly larger dark outline box behind the visible door panel so only a thin edge shows, and now figuring out the extrusion axis orientation for the cab shape.

Now I'm blocking out the cab structure: adding a painted roof lip, considering A-pillar framing, sizing the hood box, and defining the lower body block that spans the chassis length beneath the cab.

I'm also working through the wheel well gap against the lower body sides, and sketching the truck bed—thinking about a ribbed bed liner texture rendered as a thin tiled plane just above the floor.

For cargo, I'm adding small details like jerrycans, a toolbox, maybe a spare tire to fill the bed, then defining the side bed walls as thin boxes flanking the bed with a tailgate at the rear.

Setting up chrome rail trim on top of the walls, and figuring out how the bed front meets the cab back so there's no gap, before sizing the tailgate panel.

Positioning the tailgate at its bone joint so it extends slightly past the side walls, then adding taillight boxes on its corners with red glow and separate reverse-light inserts. Adding a chrome rear bumper with a tow hitch cylinder, plus a fuel tank cylinder under the bed. For the cab, I'm placing a sun visor above the windshield and a hood scoop with a dark recessed opening on its front face.

Still writing hood vent louvres and rivet rows along the hood edges, then positioning the grille plane on the front lower body with its texture placement.

Adding headlights with glow bezels flanking the grille, sizing the front bumper with chrome detailing and red tow hooks, and placing small fog light glows on the bumper sides before starting on the exhaust stack rods.

Adding the light bar now with glow boxes for the housing and individual light faces, plus mounting legs on the roof, and I'm starting on an antenna rod.

Then I'm adding a small pennant flag at the antenna tip and sketching out a roll cage with arch rods and a connecting top bar.

Still laying out the arch structure and cross bars...

Now I'm moving to the chassis, defining rails and crossmembers with their box dimensions and positions, keeping colors distinct from the tires and hubs.

I'm sketching in the fuel tank, engine block, transmission, driveshaft, and underbody skid plate, nudging positions so they don't clip through the axle or chassis rails. I'm also adding the underbody pan beneath the body, adjusting its vertical placement so it clears the rails by a small gap rather than overlapping.

Now I'm working through the suspension geometry - fitting coiled shocks between the axle and pan with the right length and pitch, placing mounting brackets at each end, and checking that the shock springs clear the inner tyre wall.

Next I'm moving on to window textures, setting up a pixel texture generator for glass panels with a dark border and a bluish dithered gradient fill.

I'm stamping a helmet silhouette into the side window texture, and now working out which way the driver's head should face based on camera orientation relative to the vehicle's front.

For the right side, viewer's right equals +Z which is the front, so I'll mirror the placement accordingly and just parametrize a single helmetX value, building a reusable sideGlass(helmetX, helmetColor) function with a small pixel-art helmet grid using a palette for helmet color and visor.

Still writing pixel grid rows...

Now I'm figuring out the windshield texture dimensions (32x12) and planning to stamp two 6x6 helmets at specific coordinates for blue and red variants.

I also need to add the rear window texture and sketch a shared glass gradient helper function, considering how to properly import the PixelGrid type for use across the texture functions.

Now I'm designing the grille texture with vertical chrome bars, a horizontal cross bar, and a small central emblem, plus a license plate texture with a white background, blue border, and character blocks.

Now I'm figuring out placement for the roundel decal on the door or body panel, checking that its height fits within the lower body section and adjusting the y-position accordingly since the first spot was too cramped.

I'll skip the bed sponsor stripe for now, and consider adding a dirty, muddy look near the tire bottoms by randomly darkening pixels close to the ground with a brownish mud color for a weathered effect.

Now I'm figuring out whether lugs should share the same mud paint logic or stay flat-colored, and checking if the lug radius falls inside or outside the tread ring and dash band regions so the coloring doesn't clash.

Paint gets evaluated per wheel so it's consistent across the 36 merged lug boxes (432 triangles total), with texel density staying fine at this scale and normals snapping to the nearest cardinal axis. Since mergeGeometries needs indexed, UV-bearing geometries and both the box and cylinder geometries qualify, I'm importing it from the three.js addons utils path and starting to write the generation code.

Writing wheel geometry code...

Writing helper functions for boxes, cylinders, glowing lamps, and planes...

Now I'm setting up the wheel loop, defining hub positions and steering joints for each of the four wheels with proper parent-child relationships.

For the parts, I'm building the tire core as a cylinder aligned along the wheel axis with paint based on position, then generating lug nuts arranged in two staggered rows around the hub using small box geometries.

Still building out the wheel rim details...

Adding the axle rod loop for both z positions, sweeping a thin steel rod between the two hub points with rounded caps.

Now I'm adding the differential housing as a flattened sphere mesh bolted to the root bone, plus small chassis links and shock rods on each side. Then I'm starting the coil spring geometry using a spiral helper with turns and pitch parameters for the suspension springs.

Still writing spring and shock geometry... I'm sweeping the spiral into a tube for the yellow spring, adding chrome shock bodies and reservoir cylinders, then moving into the body panel assembly -- hood, doors, scoop, tailgate, cab -- using the body paint material, plus chrome window trim, mirrors, and a small pennant shape extruded from an outline.

Now I'm counting up the joints needed: chassis, steering knuckles, four wheels, two doors, and the tailgate, then adding a hood hinge joint so the hood, scoop, vents, skull decal, rivets, and hood stripe can all attach to it correctly, making sure the hinge axis runs across the body rather than along it.

Working out tailgate hinge orientation and part placement, then sketching exact box and plane dimensions for the hood, skull decal, rivets, vents, and scoop opening so everything lines up with the body geometry.

Now I'm setting up the paired door assembly, computing the door panel box, its ink outline offset, and positioning the side window plane with the sideGlass texture mapped to each side's helmet decal based on left/right orientation.

Positioning door handles and mirrors...

I'm placing the mirror glass at the rearward face, then adding a roundel decal over the lower body flames for a pop of yellow contrast.

Now I'm filling in bed details and underbody trim: side skirts, mud flaps, a jerrycan with a yellow cap and handle, a toolbox with a latch, and a spare tire lying flat in the bed, all positioned to clear the roll cage uprights. I'm also adding the rear license plate on the bumper and confirming the "13" roundel works alongside the door graphics.

Next I work out taillight placement against the tailgate's back face, adding a reverse light too, then tally up the part count—around 40 pieces just for the wheels—and decide to pad out detail further with rivets, hinges, louvres, and hanging mud flaps behind the rear tires to hit the richness the brief calls for.

Mapping overall body dimensions (height, length, width) and settling on skip decisions for sponsor text and flap attachments, I start writing the color-snapping helper and the red paint palette, then move into defining the tire paint function that samples each cell's position to determine coloring.

Writing tire paint logic...

Defining the glass color palette...

Writing windshield texture code...

Right side passenger blue, using the color param. For the rear window I'm just filling with glass texture. Now I'm setting up the skull pixel art with an ink and bone palette, and starting on digit/roundel glyph patterns using small pixel grids for numbers like 1 and 3.

Still writing roundel texture...

Now I'm moving to the license plate texture, filling a bordered rectangle with blue trim and cream background, then stamping digit glyphs onto it.

Next I'm defining a ribbed floor tile pattern using horizontal color bands, then applying it to a textured box for the chassis floor, followed by building out crossbars, rivet loops, and hood bolt details.

Now I'm shaping the hood's front face position and starting to compose the final structure. I need bodyPaint to reference face normals for distinguishing the hood scoop's top faces from the rest, and I'm setting up the color palette and careful typing for tuple-based loops. I'm also extruding the cab shape from a polygon outline with set thickness, centering it along the vehicle's width, while considering whether the point winding order needs to be counter-clockwise.

Adding small marker lights, bumper, and bed rail details...

I'm keeping the flat color palette tight, settling on a small set of steel, chrome, and ink tones plus the yellow spring accent to stay under the color budget.

Now I'm defining the spike helper for the flame glow and setting up the hood joint position before assembling everything and returning the finished root bone.
